newsitem.title: UK: Staveley to focus on services for growth.
newsitem.headline: Staveley to focus on services for growth.

text.p: British engineering group Staveley Industries Plc, which issued a profits warning at the end of January and initiated a strategic review, on Monday said its services businesses would be the principle focus for growth.
A development programme, including appropriate acquisitions, is being pursued.

"The recent strategic review has confirmed the board's belief that increasing the focus on our Services businesses will create excellent prospects for sustainable profitable growth," said chairman Harry Tuley in a statement.

Staveley Services provides technical services to industry in the UK and North America, and has grown substantially over the past few years in building services maintenance, non-destructive testing and oil analysis services.

Following the review, a divestment programme has been initiated for Staveley Measurement on completion of which "a stronger balance sheet and more focused approach is expected to enhance significantly the growth rate of the Services business".

The group also said it continues to explore opportunities to "enhance shareholder value" from Staveley Minerals -- comprising the UK salt and brine businesses -- which it said is a strong contributor to the group's results.

It will implement cost reductions in the group's management structure, identifying annual savings of approximately three million stg, involving one-off exceptional redundancy and other costs of around four million stg.
On January 30, Staveley warned that profits for the year to March 29, 1997, were expected to be lower than the 23.2 million stg posted in the previous year.
